claude_take: The sharpest split this week is between the worlds being built and the one everyone is stuck in. Google's Genie 4 and Oracle's chip-shopping spree at AI World are both bets that synthetic, simulated environments are the next trillion-dollar frontier, while a Los Angeles jury is being asked to reckon with what a decade of very real platforms did to very real teenagers. Brazil's voters and Tokyo's festival jury both quietly rewarded people who stood up to power instead of serving it, Lula over a Trump-aligned challenger, an exiled Iranian director over the regime that jailed him, even as A24 sinks a quarter of a billion dollars into fantasy escapism and actual Chinese shoppers, who are not in a simulation, simply stop buying handbags. The industry keeps getting better at building worlds to disappear into; the real one keeps sending the bill.
claude_take_title: The industry keeps building worlds to disappear into

items.headline: Google DeepMind Unveils Genie 4, a World Model That Generates Its Own Soundtrack
items.summary: Google DeepMind released Genie 4, a research-preview world model that holds a consistent, navigable 3D scene for roughly two minutes, double Genie 3's limit, while generating ambient sound and reactive dialogue in real time. Users can edit a scene mid-simulation by typing instructions to change weather, camera angle, or add characters and objects. It leans on Gemini models for visual fidelity and reasoning, with access for now limited to trusted testers ahead of a planned rollout to Google AI Ultra subscribers.

items.headline: Oracle Opens Its Cloud to Google's TPUs, OpenAI's In-House Chip and Cerebras
items.summary: At its AI World conference, Oracle said it will add Google TPUs, OpenAI's new Jalapeño inference chip, and Cerebras hardware to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, making it the first major hyperscaler besides Google to offer TPUs. Oracle is also embedding ChatGPT and Codex directly into its Fusion, NetSuite and database products through a new AI Workspace. The company framed the move as giving customers more chip choice rather than a retreat from Nvidia, though the new silicon will not roll out until 2027.

items.headline: Tokyo International Film Festival Opens 39th Edition, Set to Honor Exiled Iranian Director Mohammad Rasoulof
items.summary: The 39th Tokyo International Film Festival opened October 26 for a ten-day run, with filmmaker Rolf de Heer presiding over the main competition jury. Exiled Iranian director Mohammad Rasoulof, jailed twice in Iran and honored at Cannes for The Seed of the Sacred Fig, will receive the festival's Kurosawa Akira Award alongside Japanese director O Mipo. The honor underscores Tokyo's growing role spotlighting filmmakers who have worked under direct political pressure.

items.headline: A24's Elden Ring Adaptation Becomes the Studio's Most Expensive Film Ever
items.summary: Alex Garland's film adaptation of the video game Elden Ring has wrapped production with a budget reported to be well over 100 million dollars, by far A24's biggest financial bet, dwarfing the studio's prior record-holder Marty Supreme at roughly 70 million. The project, made with Bandai Namco and Game of Thrones author George R.R. Martin, is scheduled for release in March 2028 and signals A24's growing ambition to compete on blockbuster-scale filmmaking.

items.headline: Lula Wins Brazil's Presidential Runoff, Defeating a Trump-Aligned Challenger
items.summary: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Brazil's October 25 presidential runoff with about 51.8 percent of the vote, securing a fourth term over Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro and an ally of Donald Trump. Flávio had led the first round and most pre-election polling, making the result a surprise that keeps Brazil's leftist government in power through 2027. He has said he will contest the result in court.

items.headline: Meta and Snap Head to a New Trial Over Alleged Teen Social Media Harm
items.summary: Jury selection began October 28 in a Los Angeles trial accusing Meta and Snap of designing their platforms to be addictive and harmful to young users, after TikTok and YouTube settled before trial. It is the first time Snap has been named as a defendant in this wave of litigation, with opening statements set for November 4 and testimony expected from Mark Zuckerberg, Instagram chief Adam Mosseri, and Snap CEO Evan Spiegel.

items.headline: Europe's Luxury Giants Lose Roughly $350 Billion in Value as China Demand Stays Weak
items.summary: LVMH, Hermès, Kering and peers have together shed around 350 billion dollars in market value this year, intensified by a fresh round of disappointing third-quarter results tied to weak Chinese consumer spending, a property-sector slump, and a crackdown on wealthy spenders. LVMH shares alone are down roughly 37 percent in 2026, putting the group at risk of dropping out of Europe's ten most valuable companies for the first time in nearly a decade. Richemont is the lone major holdout, buoyed by resilient jewelry and watch demand.

items.headline: Large Study Finds a Child's Own Genes, Not Parents', Mainly Drive ADHD Traits
items.summary: A new analysis published in Behavior Genetics found little evidence that parents pass on ADHD-related traits to children indirectly through the home environment they create, with a child's own inherited genetics the main driver of ADHD traits by mid-childhood. One exception emerged: a mother's genetic predisposition toward neuroticism was linked to her child's ADHD traits even after accounting for direct genetic transmission. The findings complicate simple narratives about parenting style or household environment causing ADHD.

items.headline: Levinas's Face of the Other
items.headline_fr: Le visage de l'Autre chez Levinas
items.summary: Emmanuel Levinas argued that encountering another person's face generates an immediate, pre-rational ethical demand, a call that precedes and grounds all later reasoning about rights or duties. For Levinas, ethics is not a system we choose to apply but an obligation imposed on us simply by standing before another human being whose vulnerability we can never fully grasp or reduce to our own categories. The idea remains influential wherever people debate what we owe to strangers, refugees, or anyone cast as fundamentally other, including, increasingly, debates over how machines should recognize human dignity.
items.summary_fr: Pour Emmanuel Levinas, le visage d'autrui impose une exigence éthique immédiate, antérieure à toute raison : avant même de penser, nous sommes déjà responsables de l'autre. Cette responsabilité n'est pas un choix ni un contrat social, mais une obligation qui surgit du simple fait de se trouver face à un visage humain, irréductible à nos catégories et à notre compréhension. Cette pensée continue d'éclairer les débats contemporains sur ce que nous devons aux étrangers, aux réfugiés, à quiconque est perçu comme radicalement « autre ».
